Synopsis:
PM Giorgia Meloni's government becomes Italy's longest-serving since 1946, surpassing 1,000 days on September 4, 2026. The article contextualizes this milestone with a statistical breakdown of Italy's post-war political history: 68 governments, 31 PMs, ~14-month average cabinet lifespan. Structural factors (proportional representation, bicameral confidence requirements) historically drove instability, though Christian Democrat dominance provided underlying continuity. Meloni has pledged a new electoral reform ahead of 2027 elections aimed at greater stability.
